e86c943a09828a9f: KUALA LUMPUR: Police recorded 199 criminal cases involving Rohingya refugees in the country between 2022 and August 2026.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said Selangor recorded the highest number of cases at 58, followed by Kedah with 26 and Kuala Lumpur with 22.
"2022 recorded the highest number of cases at 52, followed by 43 in 2023, 37 in 2024, 29 in 2025 and 38 up to August 2026," he said in a written reply published on the Parliament portal today.

He was responding to Datuk Adnan Abu Hassan (BN-Kuala Pilah), who asked for the number of criminal offences involving Rohingya refugees by state, as well as the government's measures to strengthen control, registration and monitoring of the community to ensure public safety and order.

Saifuddin said National Security Council (NSC) Directive No. 23, on the Policy and Mechanism for the Management of Refugees and Asylum Seekers, was established to manage all groups of refugees and asylum seekers in Malaysia comprehensively, rather than focusing solely on the Rohingya community.
He said the directive outlined guidelines and the functions and roles of various ministries and enforcement agencies to safeguard national security.

"Under the framework of NSC Directive No. 23, the government is strengthening control and monitoring of all refugee communities, including the Rohingya, through the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) programme," he said.

He added that the DPP programme served as the government's main instrument to take over and strengthen the centralised management of refugee data, reducing its full dependence on the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).
"Migrants whose status has been verified will be issued a special pass in the form of a card known as the DPP card.

"The card serves as an official identity document for this group and is the only document recognised by the government that allows its holders to reside temporarily in Peninsular Malaysia until a final arrangement is made for them," he said.

ee2f518d244240c1: SEREMBAN, Oct 16 — A Road Transport Department (JPJ) officer was killed and another seriously injured in a crash involving a JPJ vehicle and two lorries on the North-South Expressway southbound near the Senawang exit last night, Sinar Harian reported.
The accident occurred at about 10.50pm when the officers were believed to be inspecting a lorry on the emergency lane, the Malay daily reported.
A second lorry travelling behind them is believed to have lost control before crashing into the JPJ sport utility vehicle (SUV) and the lorry being inspected.
No official statement had been issued by the authorities at the time of reporting.
However, a senior Negeri Sembilan JPJ officer confirmed that one of the department’s personnel had died in the crash.
1df3a2bec0d12bd0: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — A 27-year-old swimming coach has been arrested on suspicion of drug trafficking after police seized drugs worth RM6.8 million in two raids in Melaka and Johor, Berita Harian reported.

Jasin district police chief Superintendent Lee Robert said the suspect was detained at the Lipat Kajang toll area at about 11.30am on Wednesday during a roadblock conducted by the district police headquarters’ traffic investigation and enforcement division and narcotics crime investigation division.

Police became suspicious of the suspect’s behaviour before stopping the Toyota Vios he was driving. A search uncovered 3.70g of suspected ketamine and 27.50kg of MDMA (3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine), packaged in drink-juice sachets and sealed inside two boxes, the Malay daily reported.

Lee reportedly said that preliminary investigations and information obtained from the suspect led police to conduct a follow-up operation in Johor with the state’s narcotics crime investigation department.
The operation identified the suspected drug supply source and storage location, he said at a press conference at the Jasin district police headquarters yesterday.

According to Berita Harian, the suspect, who is from Johor, allegedly packaged the drugs himself in drink-juice sachets before distributing them to entertainment centres at prices ranging from RM300 to RM600 per sachet.
Lee said the total value of drugs seized in both raids was estimated at RM6.808 million. Police also seized various equipment believed to have been used to package the drugs.
A urine screening test found the suspect positive for ketamine. He is believed to have been involved in the activity since early this year, Lee said.
The suspect has been remanded for seven days until October 21 to assist investigations under Section 39B and Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
Police are still working to identify other members of the distribution network and trace the source of the drugs, he added.
fb7669cc51f3d41c: PETALING JAYA: Ahli Parlimen Kepong, Lim Lip Eng membidas Jabatan Penjara mengarahkan Najib Razak tidak mendedahkan syarat tahanan rumahnya di bawah pengampunan bersyarat yang diperkenankan Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
Peguam Shafee Abdullah yang mewakili Najib dilaporkan berkata, bekas perdana menteri itu telah menerima perintah dan syarat tahanan rumah, tetapi diarah tidak mendedahkan butirannya.
Lim berkata, syarat tahanan rumah Najib bukan rahsia negara dan tidak patut dirahsiakan, sambil menyifatkan tindakan itu "mengarut".
Wakil rakyat DAP itu berkata, tindakan berkenaan akan mencetuskan lebih banyak spekulasi liar berhubung tahanan rumah Najib dan rakyat Malaysia berhak tahu syarat ditetapkan.

"Siapa dibenarkan melawat? Bolehkah beliau menggunakan telefon, internet dan media sosial? Bagaimana pula dengan televisyen, hiburan dan kebebasan menerima tetamu? Adakah beliau diwajibkan memakai gelang elektronik atau dipantau CCTV sepanjang masa?
"Najib masih seorang banduan, bukannya orang yang telah dibebaskan. Kes ini melibatkan kepentingan awam dan boleh menjadi rujukan bagi pelaksanaan tahanan rumah pada masa depan.
"Rakyat berhak mengetahui bagaimana hukuman penjara dilaksanakan di luar penjara," katanya dalam kenyataan.
Lim mendesak Jabatan Penjara mendedahkan syarat asas tahanan rumah Najib, walaupun maklumat sensitif berkaitan keselamatan boleh dirahsiakan, tetapi bukan semua perkara perlu dirahsiakan.
"Tahanan rumah bukan percutian di banglo mewah. Jika semuanya mengikut peraturan, mengapa takut rakyat tahu?" soalnya.

Najib dipenjarakan pada Ogos 2022 selepas Mahkamah Persekutuan mengekalkan sabitan terhadapnya atas kesalahan salah guna kuasa, pecah amanah dan pengubahan wang haram membabitkan dana SRC International berjumlah RM42 juta.
Beliau dijatuhkan hukuman penjara 12 tahun dan denda RM210 juta.

Pada Januari 2024, Yang di-Pertuan Agong ketika itu, Al-Sultan Abdullah Sultan Ahmad Shah, menggunakan kuasa pengampunan baginda untuk mengurangkan tempoh hukuman penjara Najib kepada separuh dan denda kepada RM50 juta.

Pada 18 Sept lalu, Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim memberikan pengampunan bersyarat tambahan kepada Najib, yang membolehkannya menjalani baki hukuman penjara di bawah tahanan rumah sehingga 23 Ogos 2028, tertakluk kepada pembayaran denda dan pematuhan syarat lain.
Umno kemudian mewujudkan tabung bagi membantu bekas presidennya membayar denda itu, dengan pemimpin, ahli dan penyokong parti digalak menyumbang secara sukarela.
b15b81377c7a54cb: SEREMBAN, Oct 16 — Malaysia will continue to use diplomatic channels and Asean mechanisms to address the transboundary haze issue with Indonesia through a phased approach that prioritises its people’s interests and health, without jeopardising bilateral relations, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.

He said discussions between leaders and regional channels are the preferred approaches to addressing sensitive issues involving neighbouring countries, rather than legal enforcement measures or the issuance of diplomatic notes.
“We have not reached that stage yet. It is easy to talk about taking legal enforcement action, but doing so would mean we were prepared to sever relations.

“We have not reached that point, so there is no need to issue a diplomatic note. Such a note is a last resort,” he told reporters after presenting contributions to senior citizens and assistance for further studies in the Rembau parliamentary constituency here yesterday.

He said Malaysia’s position does not mean the government is doing nothing about the persistent haze, but that it is pursuing a more comprehensive approach to finding a joint regional solution while remaining ready to help Indonesia tackle the fires responsible for the haze.

“I have instructed the Foreign Ministry’s secretary-general to take this up, and was informed yesterday that a coordination meeting will be held to discuss how Malaysia can help Indonesia tackle the fires. The Indonesian government is making concerted efforts to put them out, but the task is not easy,” he said.
Mohamad said the Japanese assistance team had also been forced to pull out because of difficulties accessing the fire sites.
“Our helicopters cannot operate either, as the haze is so thick that flying would be dangerous,” he said, adding that visibility is less than 50 metres, making flying extremely dangerous.

In a related development, Mohamad said Malaysia will submit a non-paper at the upcoming Asean Senior Officials’ Meeting and Asean Foreign Ministers’ Meeting as part of efforts to strengthen regional mechanisms to address transboundary haze.
The move also aims to enable the haze issue to be discussed within the natural disasters framework, he said, paving the way for Asean to strengthen its regional response and cooperation.

The media had previously reported that Malaysia would raise the issue of transboundary haze at the Asean Foreign Ministers’ Meeting ahead of the 49th Asean Summit in Manila, the Philippines, next month, to discuss more effective regional mechanisms to address the problem. — Bernama
00daca9e9246d38b: BUENOS AIRES, Oct 16 — Argentine demonstrators clashed with police yesterday at a major protest in Buenos Aires over budget-slashing President Javier Milei’s higher education spending.
The main demonstration outside parliament by thousands of university students and staff, trade unionists and opposition activists remained peaceful.
But dozens of mostly hooded demonstrators who broke away from the crowd lobbed stones and other projectiles at the police, who responded with tear gas and water cannons.
The clashes lasted around an hour.
As a result of the confrontation, at least 25 people were arrested and eight police officers were injured, sources from the National Security Ministry told AFP.
“Let’s occupy the streets, like in France!” a placard waved by one young female demonstrator urged, referring to the ongoing mass protests in that country for better classroom conditions.
Victoria Coronel, a student at the University of Matanza in Buenos Aires province, echoed some of the French students’ grievances, including “broken things don’t get fixed.”
“(Teachers) leave us because their salaries are not enough,” Coronel told AFP.
Yesterday’s protest was the fifth over the education funding crisis since Milei took power in late 2023.
It comes after multiple court rulings ordering the government to comply with a 2025 law that requires him to plow more money into public universities.
Security Minister Alejandra Monteoliva accused the protesters of “wanting to sow chaos.”
“The right to protest is not a right to exercise violence,” she declared on X.
Libertarian Milei came to office on a promise to revive Argentina’s ailing economy and tame runaway inflation by shrinking the welfare state.
He has dramatically reduced inflation through deep cuts to public spending, which have affected public hospitals, universities and pensioners in particular.
The president, who has bet his mandate on balanced budgets, had justified his vetoes of inflation-linked spending increases by arguing that “there is no money” to fund them.

Public spending on universities fell by 41 percent in real terms in the first half of this year compared to the same period in 2023, according to the Center for National Economic Research of the University of Buenos Aires.
The 2025 University Funding Law calls for inflation-linked salary increases dated to December 2023, as well as the restoration of student scholarships and more funding for university operations.
It was adopted by Congress, only to be vetoed by Milei in a decision that was later overruled by parliament.
The government has never implemented the law, despite various court rulings, including a Supreme Court decision in June, ordering it to do so.
“We are demanding that they pay us what they owe us,” Francisca Staiti, general secretary of the teachers’ union Conadu Historica told AFP.
Presidential spokesman Adrian Ravier said on Tuesday that the law was “suspended” while the government pursued legal action. — AFP
eb3a77c950835f80: BEIJING: Oil prices edged down on Friday morning as investors weighed risks in the Middle East and possible US moves to ease restrictions on the world's "shadow fleet" of tankers.
Brent crude futures fell 41 US cents, or 0.39 per cent, to US$105.51 a barrel by 0012 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures fell 54 US cents, or 0.55 per cent, to US$97.43.
WTI settled more than three per cent higher on Thursday after a large drawdown in US crude stocks supported prices, while Brent crude was little changed.

The International Energy Agency agreed on Thursday to release more than 20 million barrels of diesel to the market, along with any remaining oil from a record release of emergency reserves pledged in March to boost supply and cool soaring prices.
Oil prices rose overnight during the previous trading session, suggesting that "investors were dissatisfied with these measures", Haitong Futures said in a note on Friday.
"What would really cool the oil market is an easing of tensions in the Middle East."

The Trump administration is considering lifting sanctions on some so-called shadow fleet vessels that have transported oil and petroleum products from countries including Russia, Iran and Venezuela, in an effort to reduce record-high global freight rates, a US official said on Wednesday.

The discussions come days after President Donald Trump temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian diesel fuel, a move that drew strong criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, European countries and some of Trump's fellow Republicans in the US Senate.
Meanwhile, escalating conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis, along with renewed attacks on ships in the region, supported prices.
Attacks around the waterway have surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it was stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month.

The Houthis fired missiles at the presidential palace complex in the southern city of Aden on Thursday, killing two guards, while the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen detailed dozens of attacks on Saudi infrastructure amid the escalating conflict.
d6fbb4f517a6f28e: NOTTINGHAM, Oct 16 — Britain’s Prince Harry and his wife yesterday carried out their first joint engagement since their surprise move back to the UK in August, with Meghan telling well-wishers: “It’s great to be back.”

King Charles III’s 42-year-old younger son and Meghan, 45 — who left Britain and quit royal duties in 2020 amid a bitter royal family feud — were greeted with cheers as they arrived in the central English city of Nottingham.
The couple then stopped to chat and joke with the crowd as well as pose for selfies, give hugs and accept flowers.
The quasi-royal visit potentially puts the pair at odds with Buckingham Palace over their status while living back in Britain.

The king made it clear in a letter released last month that their position was “akin to private citizens” with charitable interests rather than public figures and that they should not be addressed as his and her royal highness.

Known formally as the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, the last time Harry and Meghan appeared together at a public event in Britain was when they attended the late Queen Elizabeth II’s funeral in September 2022.
Meghan, dressed in a long burgundy winter coat and wearing her hair in a ponytail, at one point kissed a woman on the cheek after she presented her with a gift.
Harry, in a dark suit and open-necked white shirt, bent down to speak to one youngster and told the crowd it was “very nice” to see everyone.
The couple were in the city to visit three charities that support young people and local communities through music, film, sport and tackling food poverty.

Britain’s Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex and his wife Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, decorate birthday cupcakes during a visit to Epic Partners in Nottingham October 15, 2026.
Family rift

Following a spectacular falling out with the rest of the royal family, Harry and Meghan have sought to build bridges with Charles — but they remain estranged from Harry’s older brother and heir to the throne, Prince William.
King Charles meanwhile visited Wales, where he addressed the Welsh parliament.
Anti-monarchy protesters could be heard chanting “Not my King” and “Down, down, down with the Crown” as Charles and Queen Camilla arrived, according to reports.
Charles, who was known as the Prince of Wales until his accession to the throne, has long had a close association with the country, one of the four territories that make up the United Kingdom.
Harry and Meghan settled in California six years ago, but in a surprise move in August they returned to live in the United Kingdom with their two young children, Archie, seven, and Lilibet, five.

Britain’s Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex and his wife Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, arrive to visit the Community Recording Studio (CRS) in Nottingham October 15, 2026. — AFP pic
Private citizens

The late Queen Elizabeth II made it clear to Harry and Meghan before her death in 2022 that there was no “half-in/half-out” option under which they could pursue commercial ventures while being working royals.

A letter issued last month by the Lord Chamberlain, the most senior official in the Royal Household, said it was “well known that in January 2020 the Duke and Duchess stepped down from undertaking representative duties on behalf of the sovereign and are no longer working members of the royal family”.
“Working royals” are members of the royal family who carry out official duties on behalf of the monarch. They receive administrative and other support from the Royal Household to do so.

There are currently seven senior working royals — King Charles and Queen Camilla; son and heir Prince William and his wife Catherine, Princess of Wales; Charles’s sister Princess Anne, brother Edward and the latter’s wife Sophie.
Other working royals include several of the late Queen Elizabeth II’s cousins. — AFP
6854caf7710fef1b: TAIPEI: Taiwan's government has told its people to shun events in China next month for the anniversary of the birth of a man officially lauded by both Taipei and Beijing for bringing an end to the last imperial dynasty, exposing another historical fault line.

China announced last year that it would hold commemorations on Nov 12 this year for the 160th birthday of Sun Yat-sen, who died in 1925 but helped lead the 1911 revolution that ended centuries of rule by emperors and empresses.

Sun then founded the Republic of China, which fled to Taiwan in 1949 after losing a civil war with Mao Zedong's communists, and that remains Taiwan's formal name. Beijing has never renounced the use of force to bring Taiwan under its control.
In a statement late on Thursday, Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council said people should not go to China for anniversary events and "echo the Chinese communists' narratives".

China's interpretation of Sun "does not stay faithful to historical fact ... It uses these commemorations to promote a narrative of 'opposing Taiwan independence and promoting unification,'" the council said.
China's Taiwan Affairs Office did not respond to a request for comment.

Beijing's government says Sun is a great national hero and patriot, as well as the forerunner of China's 1949 revolution. China has not detailed what events it will hold next month for the anniversary.
In 2016, President Xi Jinping gave a speech saying Sun opposed attempts to "split the country", adding that the "complete reunification of the motherland" was a sacred duty for all Chinese.

In Taiwan, Sun is officially considered the "father of the nation" and his portrait hangs in the presidential office, though his "Three Principles of the People" political philosophy is no longer a required school text for children.

While Taiwan President Lai Ching-te and his ruling Democratic Progressive Party champion Taiwan's separate identity from China, they have been striking a tougher tone with Beijing on the role of the Republic of China.

Taiwan's government has been particularly upset with Beijing seeking to claim credit for the victory in World War Two, saying it was the Republic of China government that fought with the allies as the People's Republic of China did not exist then.
China says Lai is a "separatist" and has refused to speak with him. Lai says only Taiwan's people can decide their future.
29dbbfe1416955ca: PESHAWAR, Oct 16 — The roof of a school collapsed in Pakistan's northwestern city of Peshawar yesterday killing 32 students mostly younger than 14, and a teacher, officials said, blaming the accident on dilapidated infrastructure.
Twenty more students were taken to hospital as residents and rescuers scrambled to pull children from under the rubble. Others in the densely populated neighbourhood described a close call.
A man who gave only his first name, Sohail, told AFP that "everyone began screaming in panic" when his niece, who had escaped the building, arrived home to tell them it had collapsed.
"When I arrived at the scene, I saw around 10 to 15 children trapped beneath the rubble, with debris piled up to their necks. We quickly pulled them out," he said.
Asim Khan of Peshawar's Lady Reading Hospital said the death toll had risen to 33 by Thursday evening, with most of the victims aged between four and 14, and a female teacher.
Most of the children who were brought to the hospital have been discharged. Three children who sustained head injuries have been admitted, Khan said.
A spokesman for the emergency rescue service in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province said schoolchildren were crushed and trapped after the roof gave way.

"When the Rescue 1122 emergency response teams arrived at the scene, they found that one roof had collapsed onto another, causing the classroom below to be crushed and trapping children inside," spokesman Bilal Ahmad Faizi said.
AFP journalists saw dozens of people at the scene.
Images released by the emergency services showed rescue workers in high-visibility vests scrambling to move debris, rubble and dirt.
A senior official in Peshawar told AFP that initial reports suggested the roof collapse was due to "weak infrastructure".
"The school owner has been detained," the official said on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to talk to the media.
'Deep sorrow'
Bodies wrapped in white cloth were carried out of the hospital as volunteers arrived to help identify the victims.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed "deep sorrow and grief over the loss of precious lives", according to a post on X. "My heart goes out to the bereaved families of the children and the teacher who lost their lives in this tragic incident."
President Asif Ali Zardari described the roof collapse as a "heartbreaking tragedy".
Peshawar resident Sher Ahmed blamed "substandard construction materials" for the tragedy and called for an investigation.

"With profound grief and sorrow, I urge the authorities to conduct a thorough investigation and take strict action against anyone found responsible so that such tragedies can be prevented in the future," he said.
Building collapses are common in Pakistan, largely due to poor safety standards and substandard construction materials in the South Asian nation of more than 240 million people.
In June, more than a dozen children were killed when a roof collapsed at a tutoring centre in the eastern city of Lahore.
In 2025, 27 people were killed and 10 injured when a five-storey building collapsed in the impoverished Lyari area of the southern city of Karachi. — AFP
80945c5d906b81f8: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Thursday canceled plans to livestream the firing squad execution of a convicted military base mass shooter, reversing a widely condemned move by Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth.
The plan to make Nidal Hasan's execution public was opposed at home and abroad, with US Democratic and Republican politicians, the Catholic Church and the United Nations all expressing outrage.
The cancellation is a blow to Hegseth, who is already under fire over the stalemated Iran war and its fallout, which are weighing on Trump's Republican Party ahead of November midterm elections.
Hasan "will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed," Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform.

The US president indicated he did not personally oppose the streaming plan, saying it "might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan."

But "many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die," Trump said, adding that the execution could still be viewed in person by immediate family of the victims if they wanted to do so.
Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said Hegseth and Trump had spoken before the announcement.
"The secretary supports the president's decision, and they are completely aligned," Parnell said in a statement.
Hasan's execution – scheduled for December 3 at Fort Hood, Texas, where he gunned down 13 people in 2009 – is set to be the first by a US military firing squad since 1945.
Last week, Hegseth said that "we'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public," later confirming that the plan was to livestream the execution.
"People need to understand that...there's serious consequences for these types of things," he said.
Backlash to the plan quickly grew following Hegseth's announcement.
MOST AMERICANS OPPOSED

The United Nations said streaming the execution would amount to "torture," while the president of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops said it was a "barbaric promotion of a culture of death," and both Australia and Britain's prime ministers described it as "abhorrent."
A Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll released Thursday found that eight in 10 Americans opposed livestreaming the execution.
Lawmakers from both main US parties have said they were against it, and dozens of retired US military officers expressed opposition to the planned broadcast in an open letter.
It "will taint the honor of the military that employs it, and a nation that allows it," and "will ensure that Hasan becomes a martyr," said the officers, including more than 40 generals and admirals.
Some US Democratic lawmakers on Thursday hailed the decision to cancel the livestream while slamming Hegseth.

Representative Chrissy Houlahan said it was "as clear an illustration as any that Hegseth is dangerously unqualified," while Senator Jack Reed said Trump was "right to backtrack" but that Hegseth "deserves to be admonished for his lack of judgment."
Republican Senator John Curtis also weighed in, saying the cancelation "is the right move, both for the loved ones of the victims and for the country."
The last US military execution was carried out in 1961, when John Bennett was hanged for rape and attempted murder.
The Death Penalty Information Center says 135 troops have been executed by the US military since 1916.
Twelve of the 13 people Hasan killed and 30 of those he wounded were soldiers. He was shot by a civilian police officer who responded to the attack and is paralysed from the waist down.
Hasan chose to conduct his own defence during the trial but called no witnesses and gave no testimony, and made no attempt to deny the charges.
He was sentenced to death by a military jury in 2013.

The court that convicted Hasan was told he was opposed to the US military's occupations of Iraq and Afghanistan, and that he had spoken online with an alleged Al-Qaeda figure, radical cleric Anwar al-Awlaki, an American citizen subsequently killed in a US drone strike in Yemen.

c56e695639f1afed: PETALING JAYA: Services on the Kajang MRT line were disrupted this morning by an attempted cable theft between the Phileo Damansara and Pusat Bandar Damansara stations.
Rapid KL said it detected a rail line encroachment and cable theft attempt at 5.30am, resulting in the temporary cut-off of power supply to the area.
This allowed auxiliary police to conduct security checks and locate the suspect. It did not state if anyone was caught.
"Power supply was restored at 6.32am after the necessary action was taken," it said in a statement, adding that a police report has been lodged.
Rapid KL said waiting times might be slightly longer than expected as services recover.
06e644f746d39c95: NILAI, Oct 16 — A female officer from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM) was found dead — believed to have been murdered by her husband — at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) quarters here Wednesday night.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad confirmed that the police received information regarding the incident at approximately 8.30pm.
“The murder is believed to have been committed by her husband. The suspect also surrendered himself at a police station following the incident,” he said when contacted by reporters here yesterday.

He said that the police are currently conducting a detailed investigation at the scene to determine the actual motive behind the murder, as well as the precise time the incident occurred. The suspect has been taken to the scene to help with further investigations.

Alzafny added that the case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code, and further details regarding the case will be released once the investigation at the scene is fully concluded. — Bernama
4fafe40177596670: JAKARTA: Indonesia's stock market is no longer worthy of "emerging market" status, according to MSCI, which intends to remove it from a suite of products tracked by global investors, in a major setback likely to trigger capital outflows.

Indonesian equities are already the world's worst performers this year, struggling since January when MSCI froze Indonesia in its indexes and threatened a downgrade to "frontier" status because of opacity in ownership and trading behaviour.
On Friday, it said reforms to address those problems had not made sufficient progress and that even a downgrade to frontier status would not reflect the severity of the issues.

Instead, it put Indonesia on a path to "standalone" status, which would exclude Indonesian stocks from global indexes tracked by billions of dollars in passive investment, forcing funds that follow or are benchmarked against the indexes to sell.

"Significant concerns remain around market dysfunction," MSCI said in a statement posted on its website. "Accordingly, MSCI considers Indonesia's continued classification as an emerging market no longer appropriate," it said.
"Feedback from market participants suggests that a reclassification to frontier markets would not properly recognise the depth of the market problems."
The Indonesia Stock Exchange said on Friday it had taken concrete steps to enhance transparency and integrity in the country's capital market.

The exchange respected MSCI's independence in conducting assessments and would seek further clarification on the basis for the announcement, its chief executive officer Jeffrey Hendrik said in a statement.

Indonesia's Financial Services Authority and Finance Minister Suahasil Nazara, who chairs the country's financial stability board, did not immediately reply to separate requests for comment on the MSCI announcement.

MSCI said it would consult market participants on a downgrade to "standalone" status until April 2027 and then proceed with the reclassification unless it found clear evidence of improvement in market governance and functioning.
Standalone markets are not included in MSCI's emerging or frontier index products, which are tracked by passive funds and serve as performance benchmarks for other fund managers.
MSCI said reclassification to standalone status could occur in cases of severe deterioration in market accessibility, size or liquidity, with Argentina being the most recent example.
Indonesia has faced a series of setbacks this year, with Moody's and Fitch cutting their sovereign rating outlooks to negative, citing reduced policymaking credibility.

The benchmark Jakarta stock index has fallen more than 30 per cent this year, making it the world's worst-performing equity market, with net selling by foreign investors amounting to US$4.7 billion worth of shares.
4eb83f8cc981bb41: ROME, Oct 16 — With Pope Leo XIV recovering in hospital yesterday following his lung cancer operation, questions are swirling about how the illness could change his papacy, fewer than two years after his election.
The 71-year-old leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics had a part of his lung removed on Tuesday and is undergoing further tests to determine if he is cancer-free or needs further treatment.
In the meantime, the Chicago-born pontiff is expected to spend at least a few days recovering at the Gemelli Hospital in Rome.
In a note published by the Vatican, his doctors yesterday said a chest X-ray “showed a good recovery of the operated lung”.
“The post-operative course is progressing as expected,” they said.
A Vatican source said the pope has been able to do some work in hospital and participated in mass at a make-shift chapel on the hospital’s 10th floor.
He also met with the Vatican’s substitute secretary of state for general affairs, Paolo Rudelli, yesterday afternoon, the source said.
There were no faithful praying outside the hospital, but strung outside one of the windows, a banner read “Haematology greets the pope!”
Despite his progress, experts said the pope’s unexpected diagnosis will nevertheless fundamentally change the papacy in some ways.
“Illness acts as a crossroads in a pontificate — it either accelerates its momentum or diminishes its power,” Vatican watcher Giacomo Galeazzi wrote in La Stampa daily yesterday.
Mikael Corre, Vatican correspondent for France’s La Croix newspaper, told AFP the way Leo is perceived has shifted.
“No-one expected to be waiting for medical bulletins again so soon — certainly not with this particular pope, who was 69 at the time of the conclave” in which he was elected, he said.

When Leo’s predecessor, Pope Francis, spent more than five weeks in hospital in early 2025, the Vatican began issuing regular medical bulletins detailing the pope’s medical treatment and the critical episodes when his life was in danger.
In May 2025, tennis-mad Leo — a keen gym-goer — became the youngest man chosen to lead the Church since John Paul II almost 40 years earlier.
“He was the ‘athletic pope’ who also proved to be a great traveller,” Corre said.
“He may remain both but he will now also be a pope whose health is constantly scrutinised.”
‘Prudent’
Leo has cancelled all his audiences until October 20 and his near-term travel plans are uncertain, including a demanding scheduled trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6 to 17.
He is expected initially to have a scaled-back schedule, with fewer public engagements.
“I think he is going to want to jump right back into things as much as he can. I think he’ll push himself,” said US Vatican expert Elise Ann Allen, who has written a biography of the pope.
“But he’s also very prudent. Leo understands his limitations and he’ll listen to them,” she told AFP.
The world’s first American pope has gradually imprinted his style on the Church leadership, speaking out on some of the world’s most pressing issues, from conflicts to artificial intelligence.
He has also proved unafraid to criticise world leaders or defend himself against US President Donald Trump’s attacks.
“We’re not going to see him change his style,” Allen said.
“Scares like this have a way of crystallising things for you, of what’s important,” she said.
“He will be even more determined, I think.”
‘Eased frictions’
Some Vatican insiders think Leo’s illness might “shift his priorities”, meaning fewer trips and more appointments, Corre said.
Several appointments are expected soon, in any case.
Leo has yet to create any cardinals, the red-hatted Princes of the Church who will vote in the conclave to elect his successor.
Five heads of dicasteries — Vatican departments — have also reached retirement age but have yet to be replaced.
Leo inherited a divided Church, with liberal and conservative factions that bickered under his predecessor Francis.

While he has been tasked with overcoming such polarisation, there are those inside the Vatican who hope Leo’s illness will spur him into replacing close allies of Francis in key dicasteries with more conservative figures, Corre said.
Others expect him to forge ahead instead with diplomatic efforts, which have already “brought great stability”, Allen said.
“I think this health crisis has eased those frictions even further,” she said.
“It’s brought the Catholic Church together in support around Pope Leo in a very strong way,” she said. — AFP
262c7f9550670dd2: NILAI: The death of a 35-year-old female civil servant, allegedly at the hands of her own husband, has left her family heartbroken, particularly over the circumstances surrounding her death.

088cead90b414257: OREGON: A person with a gun opened fire on Thursday at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, wounding multiple victims, including children, before the assailant was killed, possibly by an armed onlooker, according to police.

4de004de2d52cc2a: WASHINGTON, Oct 16 — New White House press secretary Katie Zacharia, under scrutiny over her legal credentials, seemed to acknowledge yesterday that she had failed the Bar exam, but argued she was accurate in presenting herself as a lawyer.

Appointed by US President Donald Trump, Zacharia has described herself as a lawyer during television appearances and on social media, and listed herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative nonprofit.

But there is no evidence to suggest that the 41-year-old press secretary has ever passed the Bar exam, required to obtain a license to practice law in the United States, after graduating from Pepperdine University with a law degree.

When questioned yesterday by conservative media outlet Real America’s Voice, Zacharia said she had registered to take the Bar exam but was then “distracted and overwhelmed” by plans to move with her husband to China.

“We just said, ‘Let’s take this time, and I’ll take the Bar and see what happens.’ The results are somewhat inconsequential because I knew I wouldn’t need the Bar in China, and we left shortly thereafter,” she said.
In Beijing, Zacharia worked as a lawyer at a major Chinese law firm.
She explained that she didn’t retake the Bar exam upon returning to the United States due to the birth of her first child.

Zacharia said that “many people in the field” had assured her that she could “label myself a lawyer, not attorney at law...and provide legal analysis, not legal advice,” given her law degree and experience in business law gained in China.
“I was very careful how I executed this,” she said.
The Campaign for Accountability, a political ethics organization, on Wednesday called for the California Bar Association to launch an investigation.
“In California, calling yourself a lawyer without a license isn’t puffery; it’s a crime,” the organization stated in a press release.
Zacharia held her first White House press briefing on Tuesday with an unusually short press conference where she answered questions from three journalists.
She succeeded Karoline Leavitt, a loyal Trump supporter and often combative press secretary, who stepped down in August to care for her young children. — AFP
6e07720183d2b1c5: IN the workplace, communication is often regarded as the key to effective collaboration. We are encouraged to express our thoughts clearly, share ideas confidently and contribute meaningfully to discussions.
Yet, amid all this emphasis on speaking, we sometimes overlook one of the most important aspects of communication: listening.
More importantly, we forget that there is a fundamental difference between listening to understand and listening simply to answer.
Many of us listen with the intention of responding. While someone is speaking, we are already formulating our reply, preparing a counterargument or thinking about how to demonstrate our knowledge.

We may hear every word, but hearing is not the same as understanding. When our minds are occupied with what we want to say next, we risk missing what the other person is actually trying to communicate.
Listening to understand requires a different mindset. It demands that we temporarily set aside our assumptions, opinions and a desire to respond.
Instead, we give the speaker our attention and make a genuine effort to understand their perspective.
This does not mean we must agree with everything we hear. It simply means we are willing to understand before we judge, evaluate or respond.
This distinction matters enormously in the workplace, where people with different experiences, personalities, responsibilities and expectations must work together.
Misunderstandings can arise when instructions are incomplete, concerns are dismissed or differing viewpoints are interpreted as challenges to authority.
Sometimes, what appears to be resistance is actually uncertainty. What sounds like criticism may be a genuine attempt to improve a situation.
Without listening carefully, we may respond to what we assume was meant rather than what was actually said.
The consequences can extend beyond a single conversation. When people repeatedly feel unheard, they become less willing to speak openly.
They may stop raising concerns, offering suggestions or questioning decisions that deserve closer examination.
Silence can then be mistaken for agreement, when it may simply reflect frustration, resignation or a belief that speaking up will make little difference.
Conversely, when people feel genuinely heard, trust begins to develop. They are more likely to share information, acknowledge mistakes and discuss difficulties honestly.
They understand that their contributions matter, even when their opinions differ from those of their colleagues or supervisors.
This creates an environment in which disagreements can be addressed constructively rather than allowed to grow into resentment.
Good listening is particularly important for those in leadership positions. Authority may compel people to follow instructions, but it does not automatically earn their trust or respect.
Leaders who listen demonstrate that they value the knowledge and experiences of others. They also give themselves access to perspectives that might otherwise remain hidden.
No individual, regardless of seniority or experience, possesses all the answers.
There is also a practical benefit to listening before responding. Taking the time to understand a problem properly can prevent unnecessary mistakes, wasted effort and avoidable conflict.
Asking a few thoughtful questions at the beginning of a conversation may save hours of correcting an outcome based on an incorrect assumption.
In this sense, listening is not merely a social courtesy. It is an essential part of sound judgement and effective decision-making.
Of course, listening well is not always easy. We may feel defensive when challenged, impatient when conversations move slowly or distracted by the pressures of our daily responsibilities.
Personal biases can also influence how we interpret what others say. We tend to give greater weight to opinions that reinforce our existing beliefs and may dismiss those that make us uncomfortable.
Recognising these tendencies is an important first step towards becoming better listeners.
The practice itself need not be complicated. Give the speaker your full attention. Resist the temptation to interrupt. Ask questions when something is unclear.

Where appropriate, summarise what you have heard to check that you have understood correctly. Most importantly, allow the other person to finish expressing their thoughts before preparing your response.
These simple habits communicate respect and reduce the likelihood of misunderstanding.
There will, naturally, be times when we must disagree, correct an error or make a difficult decision.
Listening to understand does not require endless discussion or the abandonment of conviction. Rather, it ensures that our responses are informed by a fair understanding of the circumstances.
We can disagree without being dismissive, challenge an idea without belittling its author and make decisions without making others feel insignificant.
Ultimately, the quality of workplace communication depends not only on how effectively we express ourselves but also on how sincerely we receive what others have to say.
We cannot expect people to understand our intentions if we are unwilling to understand theirs.

Perhaps the simplest test of good listening is this: after a conversation, can the other person feel confident that we understood what they were trying to communicate, even if we did not agree with them?
If the answer is yes, we have achieved something far more valuable than winning an argument or delivering a clever response.
The next time someone speaks to us at work, we should resist the urge to prepare an answer before they have finished.

Instead, we should listen with curiosity, patience and an open mind. After all, the purpose of communication is not simply to ensure that our voices are heard. It is to ensure that understanding is achieved.

7d4cedc8396b51d4: LOS ANGELES, Oct 16 — A shooting at an elementary school in the northwestern state of Oregon yesterday left “multiple victims,” police said, with several media outlets reporting three children and one adult had been killed.
Police said the assailant had been “shot and killed.”

Sheila Miller, a spokesperson at the Bend Police Department, said officers responded to calls of a gunshot fired into a car, and that then multiple emergency calls came within minutes of an active shooter inside the school.
Officers arrived on the scene within minutes of the 1pm (2000 GMT) call and then quickly received word over the radio that “the shooter had been shot and killed.”
Miller said they did not yet know who shot the suspect, and that it may have been a bystander.
In a later statement police confirmed that “children are among the victims,” and added that at least two people were transported to a local hospital.
“Their status at this time is not known.”
Police had scheduled a second briefing for 5.30pm (0030 GMT) local time.
CNN and CBS News both reported that four people—three children and an adult—were killed, citing law enforcement.
Police had not yet confirmed that information.
CNN said the shooter was a 16-year-old male, a detail police also had yet to confirm.
Miller said between 400 and 450 children attend Silver Rail Elementary, where more than 40 staff work.
After a lockdown Bend-La Pine School District said law enforcement was escorting students in buses to a separate location, where families could reunite with their children.
Parents were anxiously waiting at the site near a church, where parent Drew Sharp told CBS News “I have faith that he’s okay and that he’ll be alright.”
Sharp said his son was a fifth grader, the highest grade in the school, and that children were disembarking from the bus youngest to oldest.
“Which makes sense,” Sharp said, but it’s just more time waiting.”
Cannot keep accepting this
Bend-La Pine Schools Superintendent Steven Cook said district officials were “stunned and heartbroken by this senseless tragedy.”
“We extend our deepest sympathy to the families and to everyone affected by this violence. No words can adequately express the grief our community is experiencing.”
Today's classes at schools across the district along with activities and athletic events were canceled, Bend-La Pine said in a statement.
The elementary school is approximately 170 miles (270 kilometers) southeast of the city Portland. It serves primary-age students in kindergarten through fifth grade.

The United States, where firearms are readily available, is a frequent scene of gun violence, with thousands of people killed every year. It has the highest rate of gun-related deaths among all developed nations.
The deadliest school shooting in US history took place at Virginia Tech on April 16, 2007, when South Korean student Seung-Hui Cho killed 32 people and wounded 17 others before taking his own life.
There have been more than 360 mass shootings in the United States so far this year, according to the Gun Violence Archive, which defines a mass shooting as four or more people shot.
“Our hearts are with the terrified children and the families anxiously waiting to hear that their loved ones are safe,” GIFFORDS, a gun safety organization, said on X.
“We cannot keep accepting this as a fact of life.” — AFP
d1e432d31f517cee: NIGERIAN producer and media mogul Mo Abudu has realised a long-held dream by opening a unique cultural centre in London, complete with a cinema dedicated to African film and Black culture.
Located near the Houses of Parliament and Big Ben, a massive concrete facade conceals the new venue — the first of its kind in Britain and Europe — marked by a sign reading "EbonyLife Place London".
Film enthusiasts will recognise EbonyLife as a leading African production company and a major player in Nollywood, Nigeria's vibrant film industry.
At 62, Mosunmola 'Mo' Abudu heads a media empire extending far beyond Nigeria.

Ranked among Forbes' 100 most influential women in 2025, she remains driven by a clear mission: "It's time to tell our own stories. I want to showcase the best of who we are, celebrate who we are. Let them see us at our very best."
Born in London, Abudu is pursuing that ambition in the British capital through a venue she describes as both "a blank canvas" and "a bit of a mad dream".
Reflecting on her upbringing in England, she said: "I could never go anywhere during my youth and watch a Black movie."
Determined to bridge that gap, she decided to bring African creative excellence directly to Europe.
"I'm not waiting anymore for anyone to take a six-hour trip from London to understand what it is to watch a Nigerian film or to see Nigerian fashion... It's right here in London."
SAFE SPACE
The two-storey complex features a bar, a restaurant and a boutique showcasing designers from Africa and its diaspora.
It also houses "Fẹhinti" — a Yoruba word meaning to lean back and rest — alongside walls lined with paintings by African artists.
The centre's crown jewel is "Amani", meaning peace and harmony in Swahili, an intimate cinema fitted with red seats, wood panelling and warm lighting.
Financed almost entirely by Abudu's media group, the London venture mirrors the upscale lifestyle complex she launched in Lagos in 2019.
Abudu, widely credited with helping usher in the era of Nollywood blockbusters, believes African creatives must take charge of their own narrative infrastructure.
"We must take responsibility for creating our own spaces."
Describing the centre as a "safe space", Abudu noted: "You can shop our fashion, you can view our art, you can listen to our music and we can tell our stories."
Access to the venue will operate via a membership scheme. She stressed that the centre is inclusive and open to all backgrounds.
CELEBRATING BLACK STORYTELLING
While the cinema's schedule is still being finalised, its mandate is explicit.
"We will have films from all parts of Africa. We will show movies that celebrate Black actors, Black storytelling. That is why we are here," said Abudu.

The line-up will span classic masterworks — such as films by Senegalese director Ousmane Sembène and Algerian filmmaker Mohammed Lakhdar-Hamina — as well as EbonyLife's original productions, works by emerging Nigerian filmmakers like Nwani Orire and Ifeyinwa Arinze, as well as global blockbusters featuring Black leads, including the next instalment of the 'Black Panther' franchise.
Looking ahead, Abudu has no intention of stopping at the UK border.
"I would love to do the same thing in Paris, perhaps through a partnership. I'm always open to collaborating with others."

95f6ef31e91a8bb6: PETALING JAYA: Bantuan sekali bayar RM1,000 kepada pemandu teksi, kereta sewa dan bas sekolah hanya memberi kelegaan sementara, dengan wakil industri menggesa penyelesaian jangka panjang bagi menangani kos operasi dan kemerosotan jumlah pengusaha.

Presiden Gabungan Teksi Malaysia, Kamarudin Hussain, berkata bantuan itu tidak sepadan peningkatan kos operasi dan sara hidup, termasuk sewa teksi RM1,350 sebulan, bahan api RM1,500 serta penyelenggaraan RM200 hingga RM300.
“Kos insurans tahunan pula mencecah RM900 hingga RM2,600,” katanya kepada FMT.
Beliau turut menggesa kerajaan menyelaraskan kadar tambang e-panggilan yang didakwanya terlalu rendah sehingga mencetuskan persaingan tidak sihat dan menjejaskan pendapatan pemandu teksi.

Sebelum ini, Menteri Pengangkutan, Loke Siew Fook, berkata bantuan khas diumumkan Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim dalam Belanjawan 2027 itu bersifat sekali bayar dan bergantung pada hasil tambahan kerajaan jika mahu diteruskan pada masa depan.
Pemberian itu memanfaatkan 38,000 pemandu teksi dan kereta sewa serta 15,000 pemandu bas sekolah.

Sementara itu, Presiden Persekutuan Persatuan Bas Sekolah Malaysia, Amali Munif Rahmat, berkata industri memerlukan pembaharuan untuk menarik golongan muda serta membantu pengusaha menggantikan kenderaan lama.
Katanya, jumlah bas sekolah berlesen di Semenanjung merosot daripada kira-kira 14,000 pada Januari 2019 kepada 10,744 pada Januari 2026.
“Pengeluaran lesen baharu belum dapat mengimbangi jumlah pengusaha yang meninggalkan industri, termasuk mereka yang sudah berusia dan tidak lagi mampu meneruskan operasi.
“Kekangan pembiayaan juga menyukarkan pengusaha menggantikan bas lama, khususnya apabila masih mempunyai baki pinjaman kenderaan persendirian dan tidak dapat memperoleh pembiayaan baharu,” katanya.

Amali mencadangkan kerajaan menyediakan pinjaman mudah melalui program peremajaan dan pemutihan bas sekolah bagi membolehkan pengusaha beralih kepada bas berdaftar serta meneruskan perniagaan kepada generasi seterusnya.

KUALA LUMPUR: An old typewriter, wine bottles and even a Vespa - AG. Deli & Charcoal Grill has the feel of someone’s home, albeit someone who takes dinner rather seriously.

With wood-panelled walls and warm lighting, this cosy spot invites you to settle in for a meal and let the evening stretch longer. The outdoor dining area is pet-friendly, so your four-legged companion can join too.
The man behind AG. Deli is Logan Terence Lòpez, who opened the restaurant in August.
The letters A and G spell “Ah Gan”, a childhood nickname. Lòpez is also the founder of Wurst, a Bangsar restaurant known for its sausages made from scratch.
At AG. Deli, the menu roams from charcuterie to the Spanish seafood dish prawn fideuà, beef nasi ulam, with grilled wagyu beef, Iberico pork and bone-in lamb shoulder adding to the appeal.
“The menu is a compilation of dishes I know people enjoy eating,” Lòpez, 40, told FMT Lifestyle.

Lòpez makes his own beef cold cuts and brings the same care to the grill: he spent seven months learning about cooking with charcoal and wood. Depending on the dish, he switches between langsat, mangosteen, rambutan and acacia wood, each lending a different flavour.
Some may remember Lòpez’s Bangsar stall, Babi Kuah Hitam. Although it closed early this year, the pots have hardly gone cold: he now offers private bak kut teh catering and promotes the dish abroad.

On Sept 6, he brought a taste of Klang to Fukuoka, Japan, serving bak kut teh during a kitchen takeover at restaurant called Sumiyaki Sakaba Ryu. The invitation, Lòpez shared, came from the restaurant’s founder, Chef Ryu Kirishima, and his wife, Erika Kirishima.
An Indian from Klang introducing a Chinese dish to Japanese diners? Now that is a Malaysian food export with a plot twist!
Back at AG. Deli, there is plenty to explore. While they currently only serve dinner, Lòpez shared that a lunch menu will be introduced soon. So, does the food live up to the promise?

The AG Charcuterie Board brings together six types of cold cuts: beef black truffle salami and pork salami (cured sausages); beef bresaola (salted, air-dried beef); beef and pork coppa (cured meats) and pork speck (smoked cured ham).
Fresh-tasting, the meats invite you to graze at leisure, while the cornichons add a welcome tang between bites.
The beef nasi ulam is a scrumptious mix of fluffy rice and finely sliced fresh herbs, with coconut kerisik adding a nutty richness, and local salted fish lending a savoury punch.
Roasted wagyu beef trimmings round out the dish, making each mouthful even more satisfying.

Although this writer is not a fan of vegetables, she thoroughly enjoyed the grilled pumpkin fern. The Siamese pumpkin leaves, known locally as “pucuk labu Siam”, are lightly charred and finished with a drizzle of olive oil and a sprinkle of sea salt.
Simple yet satisfying, this modest plate of greens more than holds its own at the table.
For a refreshing non-alcoholic beverage, try the rooibos pineapple soda from local brand, Sans. Alternatively, pair your meal with a glass of wine or a beer.
Finish on a sweet note with the decadent peach Melba, which brings together vanilla gelato, canned peaches and balsamic raspberry coulis.
With delicious food and quality ingredients, AG. Deli makes a persuasive case for staying a little longer - and coming back for more.
Follow AG. Deli & Charcoal Grill on Instagram and Facebook.

5d4735b2337001db: PETALING JAYA: DAP's Lim Lip Eng has slammed the prisons department for ordering Najib Razak not to disclose the terms of his house arrest under the conditional pardon granted by the king.
Najib's lawyer Shafee Abdullah reportedly said the former prime minister had received the house arrest order and terms, but was ordered not to disclose the details.
Lim said the terms of Najib's house arrest were not an official secret and should not be kept under wraps, describing the move as "ridiculous".
The Kepong MP said this would fuel further speculation on Najib's house arrest, and that Malaysians deserved to know the conditions that had been set.

"Who is allowed to visit him? Can he use his phone, the internet and social media? What about watching television or other forms of entertainment and receiving guests? Is he required to wear an electronic wristband or will he be under CCTV monitoring at all times?
"Najib is still a prisoner. He is not yet a free man. This case involves public interest and may be a reference for the future implementation of house arrests.
"So the people deserve to know how imprisonment will be conducted outside of prison," he said in a statement.
Lim urged the prisons department to make public the terms of Najib's house arrest, saying while sensitive security-related information could be kept secret, not everything should be hidden.
"House arrest is not a holiday at a luxury bungalow. If everything is above board, why fear publicising the conditions?"
Najib was jailed in August 2022 after the Federal Court upheld his conviction of abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving RM42 million in SRC funds.
He was sentenced to 12 years in prison and fined RM210 million.
In January 2024, former king Al-Sultan Abdullah Sultan Ahmad Shah exercised his pardon powers by halving Najib’s jail term and reducing his fine to RM50 million.

On Sept 18 this year, Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim granted Najib a further conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of the fine and compliance with other stipulated conditions.
Umno has set up a fund to help its former president pay the fine, with party leaders, members and supporters encouraged to contribute voluntarily.
ac48d96b90a50de5: LONDON, Oct 16 — A woman allegedly raped by British comedian Russell Brand more than two decades ago told a court yesterday she was “terrified” and he became “monster-like” before attacking her in a hotel room.

The jury at a London trial heard testimony from a woman who has accused Brand of raping her in Bournemouth, southern England, in 1999 when he was acting in a theatre show at the Labour Party Conference.
She testified from behind a screen so she was not visible to the media or Brand, facing lengthy cross-examination from his defence lawyer.
“I know he raped me,” she told the court as Brand’s lawyer Ian Winter suggested she had welcomed the performer’s sexual attentions.
“I did say no, I didn’t want sex. I didn’t want his dirty penis inside me. I value my body,” she said, at times sounding tearful.

Brand, 51, who is also a former Hollywood actor and was married to pop star Katy Perry, denies seven charges of rape and sexual assault involving six women from 1999 to 2009 and has pleaded not guilty.

The woman, who was the first to give evidence, has not been identified. She said she had chatted with Brand at his show, and then suggested they continue discussing a possible theatre project in her hotel room.
“He manipulated me, he disarmed me into thinking I was safe around him,” she said in court, alleging Brand then became “monster-like”.
“I thought I was sexually safe. I thought he was a gay man ... that is my error in judgement and I regret that to this day,” the woman added.
At the hotel, she returned from the toilet and saw Brand had stripped to tight underpants, she said, telling the court that “at that point I was terrified, I had nowhere to run”.
She denied Brand’s lawyer’s suggestion he had persuaded her to have sex, saying: “He did not persuade me, he seemed menacing at that point to me.”
‘I can’t breathe’
The jury was earlier shown the video of a 2023 police interview where the woman said Brand pushed her onto the hotel bed.
“I do remember saying ‘no, what are you doing?’”, she told police.
Asked in court by the prosecution how Brand responded to her, she said: “He didn’t, he just carried on.”

cf32f4307af5f522: WASHINGTON, Ocy 16 — Nine FBI employees who were fired this year—who had all worked on the criminal probe of President Donald Trump’s handling of classified documents—filed suit yesterday demanding their reinstatement.
The nine agents and analysts were all abruptly dismissed in February by FBI director Kash Patel, a close ally of Trump.
They argue in their lawsuit that the firings were acts of “political retribution” for working on the classified documents case, which notably involved a raid on Trump’s Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida.
Trump was ultimately charged with criminally retaining classified documents at the estate, where he moved after leaving office in 2021.
That case and other federal criminal charges related to Trump’s attempts to overturn the 2020 election were dropped after he won the 2024 election.

c7baecb781ff0baf: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's economic growth is expected to moderate in the third quarter of 2026 as resilient exports and investment help offset cautious consumer spending amid rising costs, economists said.
The economy expanded six per cent year-on-year in the second quarter, following 5.4 per cent growth in the first quarter, bringing first-half growth to 5.7 per cent.

Exports rose 45.5 per cent year-on-year to RM191.1 billion in August, driven by a 66.5 per cent increase in electrical and electronics products amid strong demand for semiconductors and artificial intelligence-related equipment.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid expects gross domestic product (GDP) to expand 5.2 per cent in the July-September quarter.
Meanwhile, Universiti Kuala Lumpur Business School economic analyst Associate Professor Dr Aimi Zulhazmi Abdul Rashid forecasts growth of 5.0 per cent.
The projections point to slower growth from the six per cent recorded in the second quarter and 5.4 per cent in the first quarter, following stronger economic activity in the first half of the year.

Afzanizam said the economic landscape remained resilient during the quarter, particularly in terms of external demand, although higher living costs could make consumers and businesses more cautious in their spending.
He said the producer price index (PPI), which rose 10.7 per cent in August, could signal that businesses would gradually pass on higher input costs to consumers.
"Domestic demand is likely to remain resilient, although at the same time, remain fairly cautious," he said.
Afzanizam expects Malaysia's GDP growth to reach around 5.2 per cent for the full year 2026.
Aimi said the projected third-quarter growth of five per cent would remain at the upper end of the government's official full-year growth forecast of four to 4.5 per cent.

He identified strong demand for electrical and electronics (E&E) products, particularly those linked to artificial intelligence (AI), alongside domestic investment and private consumption as the main drivers supporting growth.
Aimi said investment in machinery and equipment, information and communications technology, and data centres would provide additional support to economic activity.
Private consumption, meanwhile, would continue to be supported by a stable labour market, wage growth and government cash assistance, although higher costs could temper spending.
He said the outlook remained exposed to external risks, including potential US tariffs on semiconductors and escalating tensions in the Middle East.
EXPORT GROWTH OUTPACES IMPORTS
Malaysia's trade performance continued to provide support to economic growth, with exports expanding faster than imports in the first eight months of 2026.
Exports increased 31.2 per cent year-on-year to RM1.356 trillion between January and August, while imports rose 22.4 per cent to RM1.158 trillion.
This resulted in a trade surplus of RM198.7 billion, up 127.6 per cent from a year earlier, according to the figures provided by Aimi.

However, he cautioned that strong export growth did not necessarily translate into an equivalent increase in domestic value-add, as manufacturers also relied on imported intermediate goods and components.

August imports of intermediate goods rose 50.5 per cent to RM90.7 billion, while capital goods imports increased 37.4 per cent to RM21.6 billion. Imports of consumption goods fell 1.6 per cent to RM9.3 billion.
The composition suggested that import demand was being driven largely by production and investment requirements rather than household consumption, Aimi said.
TRADE IMBALANCES WITH US AND CHINA
Aimi also highlighted Malaysia's contrasting trade positions with the United States and China, describing them as interconnected with the restructuring of global supply chains.
Malaysia recorded a trade surplus of RM101.5 billion with the US in 2025, while its trade deficit with China reached RM163.4 billion.
The deficit with China had widened to RM159.8 billion in the first eight months of 2026, based on the figures provided.
He said Malaysia had benefited from the China-plus-one strategy, as companies diversified manufacturing and sourcing away from China amid higher US tariffs.
However, Malaysian manufacturers continued to depend on intermediate components from China and other regional suppliers to produce goods for export, particularly in the E&E sector.
This meant that stronger exports to the US could coincide with higher imports from China, reflecting Malaysia's role in regional production networks.

Aimi said the challenge was to increase domestic value-added by encouraging local companies, particularly small and medium enterprises, to produce more raw materials and semi-finished products currently imported for manufacturing.
He added that greater domestic production capabilities and more diversified export markets and import sources would help Malaysia capture a larger share of the value generated by international trade.
"The policy challenge for 2027 is not to close the China deficit with protectionism, but to increase domestic value-added," he said.

f42325b3e9bdae6c: SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 16 — Meta yesterday launched a new open-weight AI model which it claims rivals, and in some cases outperforms, similar products from leading Chinese developers.
Muse Spark Open “is the most capable US open-weight model to date,” Meta’s chief of AI Alexandr Wang wrote on X.
Unlike with so-called closed models — such as Anthropic’s Claude or OpenAI’s ChatGPT — developers can download the parameters, or weights, of an open-weight model and then customise it.
Chinese developers have emerged as dominant players in the open-weight market for AI models over the past couple of years.
Alibaba’s Qwen, Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 and Z.ai’s GLM models have been considered open-weight frontrunners globally, but Meta claims its new open model now competes on a similar level.

“Built for coding and agentic work,” Muse Spark Open “excels at long-horizon tasks, complex software engineering, and multi-step reasoning,” Meta said in a blogpost, adding that “strong safeguards” have been integrated into the new model.
Muse Spark Open is also “optimised” to run on Apple’s advanced M5 Ultra chips, Meta said, signalling an unusual partnership between the two tech giants.
Meta boss Mark Zuckerberg wrote on X that the new model “runs great on new Mac Studios thanks to work” with Apple and its new CEO John Ternus.

Ternus, who took over as Apple’s chief from Tim Cook in September, responded that it is “amazing to run a model of Muse Spark Open’s caliber and scale this efficiently, right from your desk. Mac Studio keeps pushing the boundaries of on-device AI!”
Muse Spark Open still requires significant computing power, though.
Users can run the model on two Mac Studios with M5 Ultra chips to create a “supercomputer” on their own desktop, Meta said.
The launch comes just days after Meta announced its newest closed model.
On Monday, the company unveiled two new “frontier” models called Wonder and Wonder Full, which the company claimed rival the most advanced versions of ChatGPT and Claude.
Meta’s AI efforts were initially focused on open models, but more recently Zuckerberg has pushed the company to compete with OpenAI and Anthropic.
Meta launched its Spark model in April, marking a departure from its open-source model known as Llama, which lagged behind the rest of the industry. — AFP
8ba4f5f7eae877dc: NEW YORK, Oct 16 — Google announced yesterday it will start displaying links to websites and articles more prominently and higher up in search results powered by artificial intelligence (AI), as brands and news publishers warn of a sharp decline in their traffic.
The Alphabet subsidiary began integrating more AI features in its search results over two years ago.
In May 2024 it launched AI Overviews, where Google generates summarised answers to search queries, rather than only showing links as it historically did.
Then in March 2025 Google added AI Mode which opens in a separate window and provides a more comprehensive answer and more links than AI Overviews.
Now, contextual links will be featured more “more frequently” and higher up in AI-generated search content.
Google will also expand worldwide its link “carousel,” which are cards displayed directly below AI Overviews that show headlines with images for relevant articles.

The algorithm will prioritise articles from sites a user has previously identified as “preferred sources,” and it will also be able to pull in content from relevant social media posts and other forums.
Google will also make links displayed at the end of AI-generated summaries “more engaging and prominent” for users who want to “dig deeper.”
During its second quarter 2025 results, Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai said that AI Overviews had more than two billion monthly users in over 200 countries.
Several studies have shown that replacing traditional search with AI summaries significantly reduces the rate at which users open the suggested links.
According to a report by consultancy Chartbeat, news website publishers saw a 40 per cent drop in traffic coming from Google between July 2025 and July 2026.
In August, Apig, a group representing daily newspapers in France, alerted the Competition Authority that AI summaries were in breach of agreements reached with news publishers in 2022. — AFP
